topic: whether a TCP close can collapse to three packets
run1_quote: does not collapse, because a half-close is meaningful.
run2_quote: When it has nothing left, stacks do merge them and you get a three-packet close.
basis: The passive closer commonly merges its ACK of the peer's FIN with its own FIN into one segment when it has no more data to flush, producing a 3-packet close; the 4-packet form only holds when that merge isn't legal yet.

basis: git branch -D does delete the branch's own reflog (run-2 correct on that), but HEAD's reflog independently retains a commit reference for a checked-out branch, giving a real ~30-day recovery window via gc.reflogExpireUnreachable (run-1's figure); both framings are individually defensible depending on which reflog is meant.

topic: does an unread HTTP response body self-heal via timeout
run1_quote: hold the socket until the body is consumed or dumped, so an early `return` after checking `res.status` leaks one socket per request.
run2_quote: an undici response body you never read is freed when `bodyTimeout` fires, 5 minutes by default
basis: undici/Node return a connection to the pool only once the response body is consumed or explicitly destroyed; bodyTimeout guards a stalled in-progress transfer, not an already-received-but-never-touched body, so an unread body is a persistent leak, not one bounded by a timeout.

topic: whether EMFILE on accept() itself crashes the process
run1_quote: which is why the fatal error usually surfaces from your own code (an `open` or an outbound `socket`) rather than from the listener.
run2_quote: an EMFILE from `accept()` arrives as an `'error'` event on the HTTP server, and an `'error'` event with no listener becomes an uncaught exception
basis: libuv keeps a reserved spare descriptor specifically so a pending accept() degrades gracefully (accept-then-close) under EMFILE; Node's server 'error' event on accept fires only when that fallback is unavailable, so the fatal crash typically originates from application-level open/connect calls, not accept() itself.
